## Findings
- claim-1: In \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), \(q=n-r\), the Schur classes \(\bar s_\lambda\) with \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\) form the quotient Schur basis. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-218]
- claim-2: The Hopf antipode satisfies \(S(s_\lambda)=(-1)^{|\lambda|}s_{\lambda'}\), and hence \(\sum_{\alpha,\beta}(-1)^{|\alpha|}c_{\alpha,\beta}^{\nu}s_{\alpha'}s_\beta=0\) for \(\nu\ne\varnothing\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 702-736]
- claim-3: For every \(\rho\subseteq b^a\), \[ [\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}] =(-1)^{|\rho|} [\bar s_{(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{\,j-b})}] \quad\text{in }Q:=J_v/A_+J_v . \tag{SC} \]
- claim-4: For \((i,j,a,b)=(2,3,2,2)\), (SC) gives \[ [222]=[222],\ [2221]=-[322],\ [2222]=[332],\ [22211]=[422],\ [22221]=-[432],\ [22222]=[442], \] matching complete integral relation-lattice computations; the degree blocks have determinants \(1,-1,-1,-1,1\). [artifact b525c6b69aec42dfda85ba9b819a6a11265e17552b8c81c742e5f276ef669fc4]
## Strategy
Let \(q=n-r\), \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), \(A_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}A_d\), and \(Q=J_v/A_+J_v\); \([x]\) denotes the class of \(x\in J_v\) in \(Q\). For \(\rho=(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_a)\subseteq b^a\), padded by zeros, put
\[
\rho'_t=\#\{u:\rho_u\ge t\}\quad(1\le t\le b).
\]
The intended equation is
\[
\boxed{\;
[\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}]
=(-1)^{|\rho|}
[\bar s_{(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{\,j-b})}]
\quad\text{in }Q.\;}
\tag{SC}
\]
Here \(b\le j\), so the right-hand sequence is a partition. If \(\rho=\varnothing\), both sides are \([\bar s_{i^j}]\). If \(a=0\), only \(\rho=\varnothing\) occurs, so (SC) is tautological. The source-valid range has \(i,j,b\ge1\), hence does not include \(b=0\).

The accepted finite computation verifies the convention for
\((i,j,a,b)=(2,3,2,2)\):
\[
[222]=[222],\ [2221]=-[322],\ [2222]=[332],\
[22211]=[422],\ [22221]=-[432],\ [22222]=[442],
\]
with degree-block determinants \(1,-1,-1,-1,1\).

## Gaps
The universal certificate is not established. The needed integral congruence
\[
s_{(i^j,\rho)}-(-1)^{|\rho|}
s_{(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b})}
\in
\sum_{\lambda\subsetneq\rho}
\Lambda_{|\rho|-|\lambda|}s_{(i^j,\lambda)}
\tag{1}
\]
has not been derived from a specified bordered Jacobi–Trudi determinant. The accepted Hopf identity supplies signed products, but no proved algebraic passage from it to (1). The finite computation cannot establish (SC) for all \(\rho\).

## Next
Supply a fully ordered bordered Jacobi–Trudi matrix whose zero determinant expands to (1), including its boundary minors and sign \((-1)^{|\rho|}\); then map (1) to \(Q\), where every summand on the right lies in \(A_+J_v\).
